title: Brain imaging generation with latent diffusion models
evidence: Reports FID but does not state the reference set size. Mentions training on 31,740 UK Biobank participants; no subject count is given for the FID reference. No statement on patient-level splitting or on whether the reference overlaps training data.

title: Medical Diffusion: denoising diffusion probabilistic models for 3D medical image generation
evidence: Excluded from the distributional-metric counts: uses MS-SSIM, expert reader studies and a downstream segmentation task rather than a distributional distance. Retained in the table to show that avoiding the metric avoids the problem.

title: Beware of diffusion models for synthesizing medical images
evidence: Reports FID in a results table without stating the reference set size or composition. Subject counts are given at dataset level (BRATS21: 1,251 subjects, 1,195 train / 56 test) but not for the FID reference. Splits are explicitly subject-level. Notably, the paper itself argues FID is unsuitable for detecting training-image reproduction.

title: Conditional diffusion models for semantic 3D brain MRI synthesis
evidence: Gives dataset counts (1,688 images, 1,500 after outlier removal, 1,292 train / 208 test) but never states the FID reference size, the number of distinct patients behind it, or whether the image-level split respects patient boundaries.

title: Feature extraction for generative medical imaging evaluation
modality: liver CT, chest X-ray, brain MRI, cardiac MRI
evidence: States FDs were computed 'between the entire real dataset and 50,000 generated images', so the reference size is implicit but not enumerated per dataset. Slice selection is algorithmic ('excluding slices with less than 15% nonzero pixels') but no subject-level quota or randomisation is described. No subject counts, no statement on patient-level splits. This is an evaluation-methodology paper, which makes the omission more notable than in a generation paper.

title: XReal: realistic anatomy and pathology-aware X-ray generation
evidence: Reports FID with no reference-set size, no subject count and no selection procedure. Uses 'the official test split' for evaluation but does not state whether that split is patient-disjoint. The paper argues FID is ineffective for medical applications while still reporting it.

title: Assessing the distributional fidelity of synthetic chest X-rays
evidence: The only paper in the sample that states the overlap explicitly, and does so as a design choice: 'the MediGAN model is pre-trained on the same ChestX-ray14 database, providing a controlled setting for our evaluation.' Reference size stated for the CIFAR10/MNIST sanity checks (1000 each) but not for the chest X-ray evaluation. No subject counts.

title: BrainMRDiff: anatomically consistent brain MRI synthesis
evidence: Partitions at subject level ('training (1022), validation (113), and testing (116) subsets') but does not state how many images or subjects form the reference distribution for the MMD, nor how they were selected.

title: Frequency-aware diffusion model for multi-modal MRI synthesis
evidence: Splits are subject-level (80/10/10 subjects). States '70 axial 2D slices containing brain tissue' were selected per subject from 10 test subjects, but does not state whether all 700 slices or a subset form the FID reference, nor the selection rule for the reference itself.

title: Perceptual evaluation of GANs and diffusion models for generating X-rays
evidence: Deliberately avoids FID: 'Most existing studies evaluate these models using proxy metrics like Frechet Inception Distance (FID), which do not capture radiological fidelity.' Uses 160 real MIMIC-CXR images for the reader study; no subject count, no selection rule, no patient-level split statement.
